conventions.commits: GPG signed, DCO signed off, conventional commits (feat:, fix:, docs:, etc.)
conventions.testing: Unit tests in language module files; integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ using common::call_tool_raw and tempfile::NamedTempFile
conventions.linting: cargo clippy -- -D warnings; enforced workspace lints: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test-code exemptions via cfg_attr)

patterns: Each language handler is a module in crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/ with SPDX header and five query constants
CALL_QUERY captures call sites (free calls, method calls, static calls) with @call capture
REFERENCE_QUERY captures type references; IMPORT_QUERY captures use/import statements
DEFUSE_QUERY captures local declarations, assignments, and identifier reads for def-use analysis
extract_inheritance() handler walks class/interface nodes to extract extends/implements clauses
Language registration requires entries in EXTENSION_MAP (lang.rs), get_language_info() and get_ts_language() (languages/mod.rs)
Tree-sitter workspace dependencies pinned in root Cargo.toml; crate re-exported in languages/mod.rs

approaches.name: Full OO Integration with All Handlers
approaches.description: Add php.rs with all five query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY covering function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration; CALL_QUERY for function_call_expression, member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression; REFERENCE_QUERY for type nodes; IMPORT_QUERY for namespace_use_declaration; DEFUSE_QUERY for assignment, augmented_assignment, variable_name reads). Implement extract_inheritance() walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Wire into get_language_info() and get_ts_language() in mod.rs, add 'php' to EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages() in lang.rs, add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 to workspace dependencies and crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml. Unit tests for query compilation, element matching, inheritance happy path and no-clause edge case. Integration test covering PHP-only and HTML-mixed template.
pros: Mirrors existing OO language patterns (Java, Swift, Kotlin) exactly
Full feature parity: extracts all declaration kinds, calls, imports, inheritance
Comprehensive test coverage reduces regression risk
Supports PHP's mixed HTML/PHP template use case via grammar's dual variant
cons: Larger initial implementation (~200-250 LOC for handler + tests)
Requires careful grammar inspection to confirm all node kinds and field names
DEFUSE_QUERY may need tuning for PHP's variable_name structure

approaches.name: Minimal Handler with Deferred DEFUSE_QUERY
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY only; set DEFUSE_QUERY to None in LanguageInfo. Implement extract_inheritance(). Wire into registry. Unit tests for the four queries. Defer DEFUSE_QUERY implementation to a follow-up issue citing that def-use analysis is not yet a consumer per #1807.
pros: Defers risk of DEFUSE_QUERY tuning to a separate issue
cons: Incomplete feature set: no def-use analysis for PHP code
Violates consistency with Java, Python, Rust, Swift (all have DEFUSE_QUERY)
Issue acceptance criteria explicitly require DEFUSE_QUERY

approaches.name: Phased Integration: Core Queries First, Then Inheritance
approaches.description: Phase 1: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY; set extract_inheritance to None. Wire into registry. Phase 2 (follow-up PR): Add extract_inheritance() and update LanguageInfo. This separates declaration/call/import extraction from inheritance analysis.
pros: Reduces scope of initial PR review
Inheritance extraction can be tested independently in Phase 2
cons: Requires two PRs instead of one; delays full feature completion
Issue acceptance criteria require extract_inheritance in initial PR

recommendation: Approach 1 (Full OO Integration with All Handlers). This approach follows the established pattern from Java, Swift, and Kotlin integrations, satisfies all acceptance criteria in a single PR, and leverages the grammar's explicit base_clause and class_interface_clause structure for reliable inheritance extraction. The implementation is well-scoped (~200-250 LOC), the grammar inspection is complete (node kinds and fields confirmed against php/src/node-types.json), and the test patterns are proven. The DEFUSE_QUERY can be adapted from Java's pattern (local declarations, assignments, identifier reads) with PHP-specific adjustments for variable_name structure.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
(
  (function_definition
    name: (name) @function_name) @function
  (method_declaration
    name: (name) @method_name) @function
  (class_declaration
    name: (name) @class_name) @class
  (interface_declaration
    name: (name) @interface_name) @class
  (trait_declaration
    name: (name) @trait_name) @class
  (enum_declaration
    name: (name) @enum_name) @class
)
inheritance_walk_citation: From php/src/node-types.json: class_declaration has children field containing base_clause (for extends) and class_interface_clause (for implements). base_clause children are name/qualified_name/relative_name nodes representing the superclass. class_interface_clause children are name/qualified_name/relative_name nodes representing each implemented interface. Walk class_declaration's children, find base_clause and class_interface_clause nodes, extract their named children as interface/class names, and format as 'extends <name>' and 'implements <name>' respectively.
